title: Leadership Styles
completion_message: ¡Brillante! Entender cómo lideran las personas es clave para sobrevivir en el C-Suite. Ya conoces las diferencias entre un líder que empodera (empowerment) y uno que microgestiona (micromanagement).

stages.title: Estilos de Liderazgo y Cultura Corporativa (C2)

parts.visual:
Los CEOs y directores se clasifican a menudo por su estilo de gestión. 

1. Micromanagement (Microgestión): 
- Un estilo tóxico donde el jefe controla excesivamente cada pequeño detalle de tu trabajo. 
Ej: The new director's MICROMANAGEMENT is destroying team morale. 

2. Empowerment (Empoderamiento): 
- Lo opuesto. Dar a los empleados la autoridad y confianza para tomar decisiones. 
Ej: We believe in employee EMPOWERMENT. 

3. Laissez-faire (Dejar hacer): 
- Un estilo de liderazgo muy relajado donde el jefe apenas interviene. 
Ej: His LAISSEZ-FAIRE approach works well with senior experts.
parts.audio: Welcome to Leadership Styles and Corporate Culture. CEOs and directors are often defined by their management style. Let's learn the key terms. Number 1: Micromanagement. A toxic style where a boss excessively controls every tiny detail of your work. For example: The new director's MICROMANAGEMENT is destroying team morale. Number 2: Empowerment. The opposite of micromanagement. Giving employees the authority, trust, and tools to make their own decisions. For example: We believe in employee EMPOWERMENT. Number 3: Laissez-faire. A French term used in English to describe a very relaxed, hands-off leadership style where the boss barely intervenes. For example: His LAISSEZ-FAIRE approach works well with senior experts.

parts.visual:
4. Hands-on / Hands-off (Involucrado / Distante): 
- Un jefe 'hands-on' participa activamente en el trabajo diario. Un jefe 'hands-off' delega y se aleja. 
Ej: She is a very HANDS-ON CEO who visits the factory floor every week. 

5. Open-door policy (Política de puertas abiertas): 
- Una cultura donde cualquier empleado puede hablar con los directivos en cualquier momento. 
Ej: Our CEO has an OPEN-DOOR POLICY, so you can pitch your ideas directly to him. 

6. Glass ceiling (Techo de cristal): 
- Una barrera invisible que impide a ciertas personas (frecuentemente mujeres o minorías) ascender a los puestos más altos. 
Ej: She finally broke the GLASS CEILING and became the first female CEO. 

7. Lead by example (Liderar con el ejemplo): 
- Actuar de la manera que esperas que actúen tus empleados. 
Ej: He doesn't just give orders; he LEADS BY EXAMPLE.
parts.audio: Number 4: Hands-on and Hands-off. A hands-on boss is actively involved in the daily work. A hands-off boss delegates and steps back. For example: She is a very HANDS-ON CEO who visits the factory floor every week. Number 5: Open-door policy. A company culture where any employee can speak to top management at any time without going through layers of bureaucracy. For example: Our CEO has an OPEN-DOOR POLICY, so you can pitch your ideas directly to him. Number 6: Glass ceiling. An invisible barrier that prevents certain demographics, often women or minorities, from rising beyond a certain level in a hierarchy. For example: She finally broke the GLASS CEILING and became the first female CEO. Number 7: Lead by example. To act in a way that shows others how they should act. For example: He doesn't just give orders; he LEADS BY EXAMPLE.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término de liderazgo correcto.

questions.question: I hate my new boss. She demands to be CC'd on every single email I send. Her ____ is exhausting. (Microgestión).
The company increased productivity by focusing on employee ____, allowing them to make decisions without asking for permission. (Empoderamiento).
questions.explanation: Empowerment = dar poder y confianza a los empleados.

questions.question: Our manager never checks on us. He has a very ____ attitude towards management. (Relajado/Dejar hacer).
questions.explanation: Laissez-faire = estilo de dejar hacer, apenas intervenir.

questions.question: Unlike most executives, he is very ____. He helps us write the code and solves problems directly with the team. (Involucrado/Práctico).
questions.explanation: Hands-on = involucrado directamente en el trabajo.

questions.question: He prefers a ____ management style. He gives us the goal and doesn't interfere with how we achieve it. (Distante/No interventor).
questions.explanation: Hands-off = no se involucra en los detalles (delega).

questions.question: If you have a problem, you can walk right into the president's office. The company has a strict ____ policy. (Puertas abiertas).
questions.explanation: Open-door policy = política de puertas abiertas.

questions.question: It's hard for women to reach the executive board in this industry, but Sarah finally broke the ____. (Techo de cristal).
questions.explanation: Break the glass ceiling = romper la barrera invisible (techo de cristal) hacia el poder.

questions.question: A good leader doesn't just sit in an office giving orders. A good leader leads by ____. (Dar el ejemplo).
questions.explanation: Lead by example = liderar con el ejemplo.

questions.question: A leader who rules with absolute power, demanding total obedience and creating fear, is an ____ leader. (Autocrático).
The tendency to hire and promote people who think and act exactly like the current management is called a ____ culture. (Clonación corporativa).
questions.explanation: Clone culture = cultura donde todos piensan igual.

questions.question: A positive workplace where different backgrounds, genders, and ideas are welcomed is a ____ and inclusive culture. (Diverso).
questions.explanation: Diverse and inclusive = diverso e inclusivo.

questions.question: An environment where employees are afraid to speak up, suffer extreme stress, and backstab each other is a ____ work culture. (Tóxica).
questions.explanation: Toxic work culture = cultura laboral tóxica.

questions.question: Assigning tasks and authority to your subordinates so you don't have to do everything yourself is the art of ____. (Delegar).
A ____ leader inspires and motivates employees to innovate and create change that will help grow the company. (Transformacional).
questions.explanation: Transformational leader = líder que busca cambiar/transformar la empresa.

questions.question: A ____ leader focuses purely on supervision, organization, and performance, using rewards and punishments. (Transaccional).
questions.explanation: Transactional leader = liderazgo basado en premios y castigos (transacciones).

questions.question: An employee who agrees with everything the boss says, even if the boss is wrong, is known as a ____-man. (Adulador).
questions.explanation: A yes-man = un adulador o conformista que nunca contradice al jefe.

questions.question: When top management is completely disconnected from what is actually happening in the company, they are living in an ____ tower. (Torre de marfil).
questions.explanation: Living in an ivory tower = desconectados de la realidad (torre de marfil).

questions.question: When everyone in a group simply agrees to avoid conflict, leading to terrible decisions, it is called ____. (Pensamiento de grupo).
questions.explanation: Groupthink = cuando la presión por la armonía lleva a malas decisiones.

questions.question: To fire someone is the harsh term. A more corporate, euphemistic term is to 'let someone ____'. (Dejar ir).
questions.explanation: Let someone go = despedir a alguien (eufemismo corporativo).

questions.question: The rate at which employees leave a workforce and are replaced is the employee ____ rate. (Rotación).
questions.explanation: Employee turnover = rotación de personal (si es alta, la cultura suele ser mala).
